source.value: The lamina $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le y  ,\, 0 \le y \le 1 \big\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

decisions.question: e-12466

source.question: e-12466
source.value:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y .$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot {x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{{y}^{4}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{y}^{5}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{6}}{24}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-8182

source.question: e-8182
source.value:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overline{x},\overline{y}) = \left( \dfrac{M_y}{m}, \dfrac{M_x}{m} \right),
$$

where 

- $\displaystyle m = \iint \limits_D \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- $\displaystyle M_x = \iint\limits_D y \, \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- $\displaystyle M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type I plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/b872242423692a20a9d50658c99d9e8cee7c9b2737fb96592bc2bc35b4f72c32.png)

So, we have 

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \:0 \le x \le 1, \: 0 \le y \le x \big\}
$$

and $\lambda(x,y) = x+y.$ 

Since we require the $y$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $x$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot (x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}xy+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}xy+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{6}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{6}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overline{y} = \dfrac{M_x}{m} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{5}{24}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{5}{12}.
$$

decisions.question: e-8183

source.question: e-8183
source.value:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area $A_D$ is given by $(x_c, y_c),$ where

$$
\displaystyle x_c = \dfrac{1}{A_D} \iint\limits_D x \, \: \textrm{d}A, \qquad 
\displaystyle y_c = \dfrac{1}{A_D} \iint\limits_D y \, \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/a7992c54f85f85cab3d9f923b8daca62c410393b364d30bcfbf5cff5efc93bbd.png)

So, we have 

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le \sqrt{1-y^2}, \: -1 \le y \le 1 \big\}
$$

and 

$$
A_D = \dfrac12 \cdot \pi\cdot 1^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}1-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{[y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }[(1-\frac{1}{3})-(-1+\frac{1}{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot \frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
